correctness.rationale: Exact Walsh eigenspaces give detector-rank n on every interior energy except rank n-1 at the even-dimensional central energy; two extremes have rank 1. An invariant direct sum of affine-coordinate functions over all Hamming layers has dimension \(n^2-n+2\), so the bright projector is exactly this layerwise projector minus the normalized central radial Krawtchouk eigenmode when n is even. Its diagonal yields the fully specified sitewise capture probabilities; weight-(n-1) detectors already lie in the captured space while the origin recovers precisely the even central vector. Strict positivity of all loss rates forces exponential decay on the reducing captured space; only protected norm survives. The standalone finite-dimensional spectral verifier was run successfully against 252 cases and 16 dimension cases. Computational evidence corroborates rather than proves the all-dimension argument.

value.rationale: An entire nearest-neighbor detector layer is a natural minimal vertex separator around a source on the n-cube; capturing a coherent quantum walker need not behave like classical separation. The exact sitewise law and rank classify infinite families with arbitrarily unequal positive detector strengths, a protected zero-energy radial eigenmode occurs only for even dimension, and adding a full antipodal shell is exactly redundant whereas one origin detector repairs one parity-protected direction. These are motivated nontrivial structural consequences beyond the general spectral projector method, rather than a finite table or routine algebraic substitution.
